findings.location: deliveryFormRules.westOfUtc.test.ts, it.each rows, E3 past row
findings.obligation: E3: a past date is refused in every time zone
findings.remediation: The past is sampled only at yesterday (-1 day). Add a row for a date well in the past (for example -30 days) at both clock moments. Non-blocking.

findings.obligation: E1: tomorrow accepted in every time zone
findings.remediation: Only America/New_York is proven west of UTC. The rule is offset-agnostic, so this is a capability limit, not a defect. Record it in the acceptance note; no change required for approval.

findings.obligation: E1 and E2: the day boundary that daylight saving moves
findings.remediation: No clock moment falls on a daylight-saving change day (2027-03-14 in New York). Optionally add one moment on 2027-03-13 late evening. Non-blocking.

findings.location: deliveryFormRules.westOfUtc.test.ts line 9 and deliveryFormRules.test.ts line 43 and DeliveryCreateModal.sourceValidation.test.tsx line 87
findings.remediation: dayOnThisBrowsersCalendar is defined in three files. Optionally move it to one shared test helper. Non-blocking; no change required for approval.

findings.location: acceptance.md Covers: A user in the Americas can save a Delivery dated tomorrow
findings.obligation: Save-path claim: Save stays unblocked for tomorrow under a west-of-UTC clock
findings.remediation: The oracle observes the rule through dateErrorOf only. getFirstBlockingError, which gates Save, is not observed under the New York clock. Confirm the rule-level port satisfies the Save claim, or add one getFirstBlockingError row under New York. Non-blocking.
